_: Name, description and badge live in src/resources/connectors.json so the console and the browser process cannot disagree about them.

shape.note: The single most important thing about Zapier: api.zapier.com is not one API. It is at least four, each with its own OpenAPI spec, its own auth model and its own scope vocabulary. Treating them as one is how a call ends up with the wrong scope and a 403 that looks like a permissions bug.

apis.actions: /actions/v1/... - stored actions and the runs that execute them. This is the one the connector's description is actually about. OAuth, scope `external`.
apis.trigger-inbox: /trigger-inbox/v1/... - durable queues that receive trigger events. OAuth, scope `external`.
apis.connections: /connections/v1/... - webhook subscriptions telling a White Label partner that a managed connection is expiring. OAuth, scopes connection:webhook:read / :write. Partner-only; not applicable to Flux.
apis.partner: /v1/... - the Partner (Workflow) API: app directory, categories, Zap templates, profile. Version 2026.7.0. Mixed auth - some endpoints take a query-string client_id, some take OAuth with a completely different and much finer scope list.
apis.sdk: @zapier/zapier-sdk - a TypeScript client that is not merely a wrapper: it documents semantics the OpenAPI specs do not, and reaches surfaces (Tables, Code Workflows, Forms) that have no spec above. Flux cannot call it - it is Node, and Flux is a C++ browser - but it is the best description of how the API behaves.

notes: The auth host is zapier.com; the API host is api.zapier.com.

`external` is the scope for the actions, trigger-inbox and connections APIs. Zapier describes it as giving access to all Public APIs - there is no read-only variant, so the narrowing has to happen in Flux by exposing only the operations below.

The Partner API uses a different and finer scope set on the same endpoints: profile, zap, zap:write, zap:runs, zap:all, authentication, authentication:write, action:run, connection:read, connection:write, connection:delete. `action:run` is the one that runs an action. Request the narrow scope when talking to the Partner API rather than reaching for `external`.

The Partner API spec writes the same endpoints WITH trailing slashes - https://zapier.com/oauth/authorize/ and .../token/ - and adds a refreshUrl. The other three specs write them without. Zapier normally redirects, but a strict client that refuses to follow a redirect on a POST will fail the token exchange; send the form the spec for the API being used gives.
Both authorization_code and client_credentials are offered. Flux is a desktop client acting for one person, so authorization_code is the flow; client_credentials needs a secret a binary cannot keep.
The Partner API also offers an implicit flow. Do not use it - implicit is deprecated in OAuth 2.1 and returns the token in a URL fragment.
Zapier's own note: a client_secret is generated but not provided, because the implicit grant does not need one. A confidential-client flow therefore needs credentials obtained another way.
These endpoints come out of the securitySchemes blocks of Zapier's own OpenAPI specs rather than prose, which is the most reliable form they publish.

client_id_auth.note: Some Partner API endpoints authenticate with nothing but an approved application's client_id, passed as a QUERY PARAMETER, not a header. /v1/apps is one. Approval is a partner-programme step Flux has not been through, so those endpoints are recorded but not exposed.

white_label.note: The other way into these APIs, and the one the billing and rate_limit claims belong to. Recorded so the JWT talk in the Actions API does not look like something an ordinary integration configures.
white_label.onboarding: The partner supplies a JWKS URL for signature validation, redirect/callback URLs, expected issuer and audience, the claim names carrying user and tenant IDs, and client credentials.
white_label.token_exchange: The partner signs a JWT and exchanges it for a user access token - a backend secret used to call the APIs, never sent to a browser. A separate exchange yields a connect token: short-lived (about 6 minutes), single-use, and only for sending the user through Connect UI or MCP authorization.
white_label.provisioning: Zapier just-in-time provisions a workspace and user the first time a new combination of claim values appears, so the partner's users never hold Zapier accounts of their own.
white_label.applicability: Not applicable to Flux, which authenticates one real person with their own Zapier account through authorization_code.

pagination.note: Three schemes across the four APIs. Check the endpoint rather than assuming.
pagination.limit_offset_meta: Actions and connections: results plus meta { limit, offset, count } plus links { next }.
pagination.limit_offset_flat: Trigger inbox inboxes: count, next, previous, results.
pagination.cursor: Trigger inbox messages: opaque cursor, next, previous, results, no count.
pagination.page_per_page: Partner API /v1/apps: page and per_page, returning total, page, pages, per_page, objects, prev_url, next_url.

errors.shape: { errors: [ { code, detail, status?, title?, source?, meta? } ] }
errors.note: Consistent across the actions, trigger-inbox and connections APIs - Zapier follows its own published error-handling guideline. code and detail are the only guaranteed fields. source can name a JSON pointer, a query parameter or a request header, which is usually enough to fix a 400 without guessing.

codes.permission_denied: 403 - the token lacks the scope, not that the object is missing.
codes.external_service_error: 500 - the failure is in the connected app, not in Zapier. Retrying the same call unchanged will usually fail the same way.
codes.service_unavaiable: 503. Spelled that way in Zapier's own spec; match their spelling if matching on the string at all, and prefer matching on status.
codes.payment_required: 402 - the run was billable and the account has no tasks left.
codes.partner_api_unhealthy: 424 - the connected app's own API is temporarily down. Retryable, unlike the 500.

errors.run_status_vs_http: Three independent layers: the HTTP status of the call, the run's `status` field, and the per-error `code` in the errors array. Checking only the first is the most likely way to report a failed action as done.

get_profile.notes: Partner API. The cheapest confirmation a token works. Returns id, names, email, email_confirmed and timezone. The response is an ARRAY containing one profile, not an object - a Partner API quirk that also applies to /v1/apps and /v1/categories.

list_stored_actions.notes: A stored action binds a connection, an app, an action key and its inputs into one runnable object. This is the catalogue of what the user has already set up - Flux should offer these rather than trying to compose an action from scratch.

run_stored_action.notes: Returns 202 with a run id; it does NOT return results. Poll get_stored_action_run. Always send an idempotency_id - see gotchas. callback_url gets the same body the run-poll endpoint returns.

list_inboxes.notes: An inbox is a durable, user-scoped queue for one trigger subscription. `name` also appears as a filter and a field but is deprecated - use `key`, which is set at creation, immutable and unique per user. Each inbox also carries notification_url: a URL Zapier POSTs to when messages become available, so an inbox does not have to be polled at all. Flux has no public endpoint to register one, but it is the documented alternative and is why the read limits here are not the constraint they look like.

list_messages.notes: Message status is available, leased, acked or quarantined. message_attributes carries lease_count, error_message and possible_duplicate_data.

list_categories.notes: Partner API, and the spec lists no security requirement at all for this one. Useful only for populating a directory UI.

params.app: required - canonical App UUID or app key
params.action_type: READ | READ_BULK | SEARCH | SEARCH_AND_WRITE | SEARCH_OR_WRITE | WRITE

list_app_actions.notes: Partner API. What a given app can do. `key` is the developer-provided stable identifier; `id` is explicitly documented as unstable and changing when the referenced app changes - never persist `id`, match on `key`. is_instant marks a real-time trigger and can only be true when the action is a READ.

params.app: required - canonical App UUID or app key

list_authentications.notes: Partner API. The user's own connections to an app. Returns only authentications the user OWNS, never ones shared with them, because a Zap cannot be built on a borrowed connection. is_expired true means the user has to reconnect - check it before offering an action rather than letting the run fail.

get_stored_action_run.notes: 200 carries results; 202 means still processing - poll again. Rate limited far more generously than the rest of the Actions API (600 per 5 minutes, override to 3000), which is what makes polling viable. Results are kept seven days.

response.results: array - can be empty even on success
response.next_page: bulk-read paging state; pass back as `page` on the next run

create_stored_action.notes: Saves a runnable configuration; it does NOT execute anything, which is why this is `draft` and not `send`. Returns 200 (not 201) with just the id. Only core actions - external and App Extension actions cannot be stored. The triple selected_api + action_type + action_key is mandatory; action_id is deliberately not accepted.

get_action_input_fields.notes: Partner API. A POST that reads - the current inputs are sent because later fields depend on earlier ones. Fields resolve against the app's CURRENT version unless selected_api pins one; pin it when editing an action built against an older version. Returns input_field, info_field or fieldset entries; invalidates_input_fields true means changing this field forces a refetch.

get_action_input_choices.notes: Partner API. The values behind a SELECT field.

get_action_output_fields.notes: Partner API. What an action returns. fetch_live_samples calls the third-party service for real samples - slower, and not supported for WRITE actions.

action_types.note: A stored action's action_type disambiguates same-named actions within one integration. It is descriptive, not a permission - none of these values make a run safe.

gotchas: app identifiers accept four forms - fully versioned (SplitwiseCLIAPI@1.0.0), versionless (SlackCLIAPI), the @latest sentinel, or a service slug (slack). The last three resolve at creation time and the object then stores the fully versioned form forever, so a stored action or inbox does not follow the app forward. An ambiguous or unmatched identifier is a 400, not a silent miss.

possible_duplicate_data on a trigger message means Zapier's deduplication key changed and the payload may repeat data already delivered. Zapier's own guidance is that consumers should apply their own deduplication - so anything acting on these messages has to be idempotent, not merely careful.

An inbox can pause itself. paused_reason includes authentication, authentication_access_revoked, partner_revoked, subscribe_failed, migrate_failed, abandoned and upstream_failures. A connector that has quietly stopped producing messages should read status before concluding there is nothing to do.
A 500 with code external_service_error is the connected app failing, not Zapier. It is not a retryable transient in the usual sense.
Partner API list endpoints return a single-element ARRAY wrapping the page object, not the page object itself. Indexing straight into .objects will fail.

Two different action_type vocabularies. The Actions API (stored actions) uses lowercase and includes run, filter and tool: read, read_bulk, write, run, search, search_or_write, search_and_write, filter, tool. The Partner API /v2/actions uses UPPERCASE and a shorter set: READ, READ_BULK, SEARCH, SEARCH_AND_WRITE, SEARCH_OR_WRITE, WRITE. Same concept, different spelling, different API - do not map one onto the other by string equality.

In the Partner API's own schema, the Action object's `type` and `action_type` both $ref the same ActionTypeEnum, but that enum contains only the single value `action` while the action_type description lists READ, WRITE and the rest. The schema and the prose disagree; the example payload shows type: action alongside action_type: action. Read what comes back rather than validating against the enum.

Partner API pagination changed between versions. /v1 returns a single-element array wrapping { total, page, pages, per_page, objects, prev_url, next_url }. /v2 returns { links: { next, prev }, meta: { count, limit, offset }, data: [...] }. Same API title, two envelopes.
An action id from /v2/actions is documented as unstable and not reused. Anything that hardcodes one will break silently when the app updates - persist `key` plus the app identifier.

An action run status of `unknown` is not a failure and not a success - Zapier documents it as the outcome being undeterminable. Retrying it may double the effect; treating it as success may silently drop work. It needs a human, or an idempotency key on the target.
Action-run callbacks are at-least-once by Zapier's own statement. Any callback receiver must deduplicate on the run id.
Releasing a leased trigger message does not refund the lease attempt against the per-message limit.
A workflow's trigger_url embeds a trigger token in the path. Zapier flags it as sensitive - it is a credential in a URL, and it will end up in logs if handled carelessly.
Zapier Forms default to consumerAuth `none`: the published hosted_url is answerable by anyone who has it.

Unversioned app identifiers resolve at DIFFERENT times depending on the object. A trigger inbox resolves at creation and stores the fully versioned form forever, so it never follows the app forward. A stored action's selected_api, per its own schema, is resolved when the action runs - 'if no version is provided we attempt to use the latest version'. Same-looking field, opposite behaviour: pin the version explicitly if a run has to stay reproducible.

idempotency_id on a run is the answer to the `unknown` status problem. It is a client-supplied UUID, and a repeat within 72 hours is ignored and returns the original response. Send one on EVERY run: it is the only thing that makes retrying an inconclusive run safe.
connection_id here is the same UUID other Zapier APIs call authentication_id - the Partner API's /v2/actions uses that name. Zapier says so in their own note. Same value, two field names, two APIs.

PATCH on a stored action cannot change connection_id or selected_api. Zapier's guidance is to delete and recreate. An update that appears to succeed will not have moved the action to a different connection.

424 partner_api_unhealthy is the connected app being down, and is explicitly retryable later. It is distinct from 500 external_service_error, which is the app returning a failure - retrying that unchanged will fail the same way.
The run path is singular (.../run) but the result path is plural (.../runs/{run_id}). Easy to get backwards.

A stored-action run has TWO levels of success and they disagree routinely. Zapier's own words: the HTTP status of the run-results call reports Zapier's processing, not what happened in the external system, and 'you could have a success=True (Zapier succeeded) and status=error (the partner raised an error)'. Always read the body's `status` field and the `errors` array; a 200 means only that Zapier managed to run the thing.

Partner errors carry their own code vocabulary, separate from the HTTP error codes: user, authentication, partner, system, throttled, system_throttled, hydration, authentication_access. When code is throttled the error object carries `delay` - the seconds to wait - which is the retry signal, not Retry-After.

Polling is budgeted differently from acting. The run-results endpoint allows 600 requests per 5 minutes (override to 3000) while the rest of the Actions API allows 200 (override to 1000). Poll freely; run sparingly.

POST /v2/actions/{id}/test executes the step against the third-party API for real - Zapier's own description says 'tests the action (step) in the third party api'. It is not a dry run and must never be used to preview a WRITE.

Getting an action's INPUT fields needs zap:write, while getting a SELECT field's CHOICES needs only zap. Two reads, two different scopes, the stricter one on the less dangerous call. Request per endpoint rather than assuming.

actions_api.note: 200 requests per 5 minutes by default, and the ceiling is set on the JWT rather than per request: rate_limit.limit_override takes 1-1000, and rate_limit.exempt true skips limiting entirely. Zapier also gates the whole mechanism behind an internal feature flag, so the absence of throttling today is not a guarantee - read X-RateLimit-Remaining rather than assuming.

rate_limits.partner_api: Stated only as a per-hour cap in the header descriptions, with no number given.
rate_limits.on_exceed: HTTP 429 with code too_many_requests and a required Retry-After in seconds.

headers.X-RateLimit-Reset: When the window resets. The actions API documents this as a unix timestamp typed as date-time; the partner API documents it as UTC epoch seconds. Parse defensively.

backoff.strategy: Honour Retry-After exactly - it is marked required on every 429 and 503. Pace against X-RateLimit-Remaining rather than waiting to be told.

not_applicable.connections_api: /connections/v1/webhooks exists for White Label partner accounts to be told, via a signed callback, that a connection they manage is expiring (the only event is connection.expiry_scheduled; the payload carries connection_id, account_id, app as app_key@version, title and expires_at). Registration is POST /connections/v1/webhooks with scope connection:webhook:write, and returns a whsec_ secret ONCE - never again, and never in the list response. 409 means an active webhook for that event type already exists. Deliveries follow Standard Webhooks: webhook-id (stable across retries, use it to deduplicate), webhook-timestamp, and webhook-signature as a space-delimited list of v1,<base64 HMAC-SHA256> over {webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}. Flux is not a White Label partner and has no public callback URL, so none of it applies. Recorded so it is not mistaken for a way to watch the user's own connections.
not_applicable.partner_app_directory: /v1/apps authenticates with an approved partner client_id in the query string. Flux has not been through that approval, so the app-directory endpoints are not exposed even though they need no user token.

also_ships.specs: Every API's OpenAPI spec is at https://api.zapier.com/api-reference/specs/<api-name>.yaml - actions.yaml, trigger-inbox.yaml, connections.yaml - and the Partner API spec at https://api.zapier.com/schema. Any docs page can be fetched as markdown by appending .md. docs.zapier.com/llms.txt indexes the lot.
also_ships.mcp: Zapier serves a docs MCP server at docs.zapier.com/mcp. That is documentation search, not action invocation - do not confuse the two.

pending_operations.note: Searched for, not found. Recorded as open rather than guessed.
wanted: The REST paths behind the trigger-inbox lease / ack / release and create / pause / resume / delete methods. Zapier documents these only as SDK methods; the semantics are complete above but no published page gives the HTTP paths. If Flux ever needs them, capturing them from the SDK's own traffic is the reliable route.

Whether Tables, Code Workflows and Forms have public REST specs. The specs directory pattern is https://api.zapier.com/api-reference/specs/<name>.yaml and docs.zapier.com/api-reference/overview indexes which APIs exist - that overview page is the one thing that would settle it, and it has not been read.

notes: Every host, path, scope, pagination scheme, error code and rate-limit figure above is taken verbatim from the OpenAPI 3.1 specs embedded in Zapier's own reference pages.
The one exception is the run_stored_action path prefix, which the spec gives only in prose. It is flagged in place rather than presented as verified.
docs.zapier.com and api.zapier.com are not reachable from the Flux container - the egress proxy refuses the CONNECT - so the remaining specs need supplying the same way.

The SDK reference supplied by the user is the source for the sdk block, the run-status vocabulary, the callback delivery guarantee and the trigger-inbox lifecycle. Those are SDK method names, not REST paths, and the file says so rather than presenting them as endpoints.

The run endpoint's path is now CONFIRMED from actions.yaml's own paths block: POST /actions/v1/stored-actions/{stored_action_id}/run. An earlier revision inferred that prefix from a sibling path and said so; the inference was right, and the caveat is removed.
The White Label token-exchange model and the lease_count-of-5 quarantine threshold came from documentation search rather than a supplied page. Everything else in this file is verbatim from the specs.

sdk.note: Recorded for its semantics, not because Flux runs it. Method names below are SDK methods, NOT REST paths; the paths behind most of them are still unknown.
sdk.install: npm install @zapier/zapier-sdk (plus @zapier/zapier-sdk-cli as a dev dependency for the CLI auth path).

auth_modes.cli: npx zapier-sdk login - the SDK picks the CLI's session up automatically. Interactive; no use for a headless caller.
auth_modes.client_credentials: npx zapier-sdk create-client-credentials, then pass clientId and clientSecret. The server/serverless path. Note this mints credentials from the CLI, which is a different route to the same client_credentials grant the OpenAPI specs describe.
auth_modes.token: Pass a Zapier token directly. Documented as being for partner OAuth or internal Zapier use.

running_an_action.note: The thing the connector's description is actually about, and it is asynchronous. This is the clearest statement of the model anywhere in Zapier's docs.
running_an_action.one_call: runAction(app, actionType, action, inputs) starts a run and waits. timeoutSeconds defaults to 180.
running_an_action.two_call: createActionRun returns a run id immediately; getActionRun fetches the outcome. Use this pair to fan out, hand the id to another process, or survive a restart.
running_an_action.retention: Run results are kept for seven days after creation.
running_an_action.vs_stored_actions: createActionRun takes app + actionType + action + inputs ad hoc. The stored-actions endpoints in the REST spec run a SAVED configuration by id. Related but not the same call - do not conflate them.

sdk.status_values: waiting (still executing), error (the app failed; see errors[]), and unknown - which Zapier documents as 'the response carried no status, so the outcome could not be determined'. Their own instruction is to treat unknown as INCONCLUSIVE, not as success. An action may or may not have happened.

callbacks.note: createActionRun accepts a callbackUrl so a finished run is pushed rather than polled. The body matches what getActionRun returns.
callbacks.requirements: HTTPS and a publicly resolvable host - a local receiver needs a tunnel.
callbacks.delivery: Zapier says to expect the same run to arrive MORE THAN ONCE. At-least-once, so the receiver must deduplicate.

trigger_inbox_lifecycle.note: Closes what was previously recorded as unknown - the capability and its semantics, though still not the REST paths.
trigger_inbox_lifecycle.create: createTriggerInbox always makes a new inbox. ensureTriggerInbox is the get-or-create on a stable key, idempotent per (user, account, key), and throws a conflict if the key exists with a different subscription. Prefer ensure.
trigger_inbox_lifecycle.consume: leaseTriggerInboxMessages (leaseLimit 1-100, leaseSeconds default 300) then ackTriggerInboxMessages. Unacked messages return to the pool when the lease expires.
trigger_inbox_lifecycle.release: releaseTriggerInboxMessages returns messages immediately without acking - but the lease attempt still counts against the per-message lease limit. Releasing does not refund it, so a message repeatedly released will eventually exhaust its attempts.
trigger_inbox_lifecycle.higher_level: drainTriggerInbox processes until empty; watchTriggerInbox drains then subscribes to SSE for new arrivals, with a safety drain every maxDrainIntervalSeconds (default 300) because SSE events can be missed.
trigger_inbox_lifecycle.quarantine: lease_count increments on every lease, and at 5 the message transitions to `quarantined` - which is where the quarantined status in the message enum comes from. Combined with release not refunding an attempt, a message that keeps failing is dropped from the pipeline after five tries rather than retrying forever. Anything that must not be lost has to notice quarantined messages.

other_surfaces.tables: Zapier Tables - create/list/delete tables, fields and records. keyMode chooses whether record data is keyed by human field name (default) or raw field id (f1, f2). Batch writes cap at 100 records.
other_surfaces.code_workflows: Experimental. Durable TypeScript workflows: publish source files, run them, poll runs. See never_expose.
other_surfaces.forms: Experimental. Create a Zapier Form and get a shareable hosted_url; consumerAuth defaults to `none`, meaning anyone with the link can answer it.

never_expose: zapier.fetch() - it proxies an arbitrary URL through Zapier's Relay and INJECTS the user's stored credentials for a named connection into the outgoing request. An agent holding this can call any endpoint on the internet carrying the user's OAuth token or API key. It is a credential-lending primitive wearing an HTTP client's interface, and no task in the Flux catalogue needs it.

runDurable and publishWorkflowVersion - both take TypeScript source files and execute them on Zapier's runner. That is arbitrary remote code execution commissioned by the agent, and it runs with the account's connections bound to it.
triggerWorkflow, enableWorkflow, disableWorkflow, deleteWorkflow - firing or altering the user's existing automations from inside a task, where the blast radius is whatever that workflow does.
importWorkflow - converts an existing Zap and creates a workflow; harmless-sounding but it writes to the account.

createConnection, getConnectionStartUrl and waitForNewConnection - these mint a signed, single-use, time-limited URL bound to the current session that completes an OAuth grant. Connecting an account belongs in the console's own setup flow in front of the user, not in a tool call. The same rule already applies to Superhuman Mail's add_account, and for the same reason.
createClientCredentials and deleteClientCredentials - minting or revoking API credentials.
deleteTable, deleteTableFields, deleteTableRecords, discardWorkflowDraft - destructive, and Tables holds real user data.
createForm - it publishes by default to a public URL.

PATCH and DELETE on a stored action - they edit or destroy the user's saved automation configurations, and PATCH cannot do the one change someone would most want (moving it to another connection), so a task attempting a fix would silently not make it.
Anything that sets the JWT's billing claim. See the billing block: is_billable true spends the user's task quota.
POST /v2/actions/{action_id}/test - despite the name it runs the step against the live third-party API. Safe-sounding and not safe; a WRITE action tested this way really writes.

billing.note: Running a stored action can be BILLED to the user, and the switch is in the auth token rather than the request. This is the most surprising thing in the API and belongs in front of anyone wiring it up.
billing.mechanism: The bearer token carrying these claims is a WHITE LABEL partner JWT, not an ordinary user token. Partner onboarding registers a JWKS URL, expected issuer and audience, a mapping from the partner's claims to a Zapier user and workspace, and client credentials; the partner then signs a JWT and exchanges it for a user access token. A `billing` claim with is_billable true charges the user one task per successful run.
billing.default: is_billable is false by default, so runs are not billed unless something opts in.
billing.flux_position: Moot for Flux, and worth knowing why: this claim can only be set by a registered White Label partner signing its own JWTs, which Flux is not. Flux therefore cannot bill the user even by mistake - and must not become a partner in order to, since spending someone's task quota is a purchase the console never asks for.
